article.title: Pet coke lands 14% dearer as cement makers head into the pre-monsoon season
article.text: Imported pet coke landed costs are running about fourteen per cent above the previous quarter's average, and diesel-linked road freight, which carries roughly a third of Indian cement volumes on the outbound leg, has risen with the institutional fuel revision. Power and fuel together with freight are close to half of the delivered cost of a bag of cement, and the industry enters the pre-monsoon quarter with realisations already soft in the eastern and central markets. UltraTech Cement, which has the widest grinding footprint and the most captive power, and Ambuja Cements, which relies more on purchased power in its eastern clusters, face the same input move with different absorption capacity. Dalmia Bharat did not comment.
article.note: Two subjects with genuinely different absorption capacity: the correct output is two primary rows with the same direction but different materiality, plus a silent peer that is not published.

Roughly a third of Indian cement volumes move by road on the outbound leg. Power, fuel and freight are close to half the delivered cost of a bag of cement, and realisations are already soft in the eastern and central markets.

shocks.label: Cement energy and freight cost
shocks.mechanism: Pet coke and diesel-linked outbound freight together approach half the delivered cost of cement, so a simultaneous rise in both compresses EBITDA per tonne while realisations are soft

companies.name: Ambuja Cements
companies.mechanism: Eastern and northern clusters lean on purchased grid power and imported pet coke, so a fourteen per cent landed-cost rise passes almost undiluted into cost per tonne
companies.rationale: Higher purchased-power and imported pet coke share than the market leader

companies.name: UltraTech Cement
companies.mechanism: Captive power and the widest blending footprint dilute the pet coke step-up per tonne, but diesel-linked outbound freight still lifts delivered cost across the network
companies.rationale: Largest producer with captive power partially insulating the energy line
offsetting_channels: captive power reduces purchased energy exposure

ground_truth.rationale: Both named producers are subjects at distance 1 with a cost-share mechanism specific to their own energy mix. The third producer is named only as declining to comment and is never proposed by the mapping stage at all -- correct behaviour is that it simply does not appear, not that it is inferred in by sector membership.
